title: Gold-standard annotation set
description: Human annotations of registry outcomes, used to measure classifier accuracy rather than mere coverage.

annotator.description: Who annotated. Named, because agreement between two named annotators is the only evidence that the vocabulary is well enough defined to be applied consistently.

guideline.description: The annotation guideline followed. Without one, disagreement cannot be told apart from two people answering different questions.

independence.description: How this set relates to the classifier. self_annotated means the same party authored both, so scores measure self-consistency and NOT accuracy; independent means annotated without reference to classifier output; adjudicated means two annotators plus a resolved disagreement pass.

concept_id.description: The correct concept, or explicit null for 'no concept in the vocabulary describes this'. Null items matter: without them a classifier can score perfectly by matching everything to something.

text.description: The measure text, copied in so the file can be reviewed without a database to hand.

source_hash.description: The outcome record_hash when annotated. If the registry rewrites the text this stops matching and the item is excluded from scoring rather than being scored against words the annotator never saw.

axes.description: Expected axis values. Only the axes stated here are scored, so an annotator may judge the concept alone and leave parameters unjudged.

difficulty.description: The annotator's own read of how hard the call was. Accuracy on 'clear' items and accuracy on 'ambiguous' ones mean different things and should be reported apart.
